Probe through the real PR 11 adapter: 1.0.0 run -> 200/200/404 REVIEW_NOT_FOUND/404 INPUTS_NOT_FOUND; re-exported run -> 200 detail with review node session_id + result_uri, 200 reviews/1 (approved, 6 findings, patch-review-2bb474561d3e), 200 inputs (mode automatic, reviewer_transport print). Tests cover the transport matrix, malformed receipts, refusal matrix and a CLI refusal that leaves the previous file untouched. Weak spots are minor: transport inferred from file existence instead of the receipt's own `transport` field, `confirmed_at` from mtime, unguarded `policy["feature"]`/`["version"]`, and ExportRuntime copying Pipeline.__init__'s checks. Merging as-is leaves the viewer working for old and new runs.
data.ranking_reason: PR 11 is the only PR where the export version bump, the export sections and the adapter that consumes them ship together and were proven compatible in both directions (legacy 1.0.0 still loads; re-exported 1.2.0 serves review and inputs), with the cleanest null handling and a single shared review validator. PR 9 ranks second purely because it changes nothing here and therefore breaks nothing. PR 10 ranks last on this dimension despite decent export code and tests, because it bumps run-state.json to 1.2.0 while shipping an adapter that only accepts 1.0.0: every new run becomes RUN_STORAGE_INVALID in the viewer and the existing run breaks on its first `status`, and its export shape contradicts its own runInputs contract for that existing run.

findings.title: Export bumped to 1.2.0 with the 1.0.0-only adapter unchanged: new runs are unviewable
findings.detail: PR 10 sets EXPORT_VERSION = "1.2.0" and writes `review`/`inputs` sections, but ships no server/ change, so the adapter still validates `version: z.literal('1.0.0')`. Every run exported by PR 10's controller (prepare already calls export_state) is rejected by the viewer with RUN_STORAGE_INVALID. The handoff acknowledges this and defers the fix to slice B's future feature run, which is exactly the split the umbrella PRD avoided by keeping the export bump inside B's run together with its adapter. Merging PR 10 as-is does not leave the viewer working for new runs.
findings.evidence: /home/agentops/dev/md-manager-high/workflow/export_state.py:16 `EXPORT_VERSION = "1.2.0"`; :124 `value = {"version": EXPORT_VERSION, ...}`. `git diff 61e4752 a1fab98 --stat -- server/ src/` -> empty. main /home/agentops/dev/md-manager/server/projects.ts:37 `const EXPORT_VERSION = '1.0.0'`, :52 `version: z.literal(EXPORT_VERSION)`. Probe (PR 10 export of a copy of project-workflows-001 served by main's adapter via tsx): `500 /api/.../runs :: {"error":{"code":"RUN_STORAGE_INVALID","message":"Run \"project-workflows-001\" has malformed or contradictory persisted state: run-state.json version: Invalid input: expected \"1.0.0\""}}` and the same 500 on the run detail. docs/HANDOFF_REVIEW_VISIBILITY.md:77 "Between this change landing and B's run merging, new runs export at version 1.2.0, which the current adapter rejects".

findings.title: Existing run breaks on the first `workflow status`, not only on `workflow export`
findings.detail: The handoff says only that `workflow export` was withheld from project-workflows-001 so the live run keeps loading. But every controller action, including read-only `status`, calls report(), which calls export_state(), which rewrites run-state.json whenever the computed value differs from the file, and the version string now differs. So the first `status`/`automatic-step` on the existing run after merging PR 10 writes a 1.2.0 export that the shipped adapter rejects. The requirement that the existing run keep loading holds only while nobody touches it.
findings.evidence: /home/agentops/dev/md-manager-high/workflow/pipeline.py:479-481 `def report(runtime, state): ... export_state(runtime, state)`; :688 status branch `print(f"Report: {report(runtime, state)}")`. export_state.py:130-133: `if previous and {k: v for k, v in previous.items() if k != "updated_at"} == value: return previous` else `save_json(path, value)` with `value["version"] == "1.2.0"` vs on-disk `1.0.0`. Handoff :76 only says "`workflow export` was not run on project-workflows-001 ... Run it after B merges"; no mention of the status/report path. PR 11 has the same rewrite but its adapter accepts 1.2.0 (probe: 200).

findings.title: Export of the live run violates PR 10's own runInputs contract (missing reviewer_transport, mode 'interactive' for an automatic run, feature null)
findings.detail: export_inputs passes `plan.get("automatic")` through raw and `mode: plan.get("mode")`. For project-workflows-001 (pinned before reviewer_transport existed; main sets mode="interactive" for every prepare) this yields `automatic` without `reviewer_transport`, `mode: "interactive"` for an automatic run, and `feature: null`. PR 10's contract requires `automatic.reviewer_transport: z.enum(['native','print'])` (non-nullable) and enumerates `mode: z.enum(['interactive'])` only, so the contract cannot distinguish automatic from manual runs and C's future adapter must invent the 'print' default that validate_automatic applies. PR 10's own test asserts the omission. PR 11 resolves both in the export (`mode: "automatic" if automatic else "manual"`, transport from receipts or null).
findings.evidence: /home/agentops/dev/md-manager-high/workflow/export_state.py:102-103 `"mode": plan.get("mode"), ... "automatic": plan.get("automatic")`; contracts/projects/v1.ts:~125 `mode: z.enum(['interactive'])`, :~132 `reviewer_transport: z.enum(['native', 'print'])` (not nullable); workflow/test_export.py:107 `self.assertNotIn("reviewer_transport", state["inputs"]["automatic"])`. Probe output of PR 10 export on the live-run copy: `inputs header: {'feature': None, ..., 'mode': 'interactive', 'automatic': {'finish': ..., 'review_timeout_seconds': 1800}}` (no reviewer_transport). automatic.py:54 `settings.get("reviewer_transport", "print")`. Compare PR 11 export_state.py:143,148 and probe: `'mode': 'automatic', ... 'reviewer_transport': 'print'`.

findings.title: Second, divergent review validator added instead of reusing the existing one
findings.detail: `validate_review_record` re-implements `Pipeline.validate_review` with different rules (regex checks on hashes, bundle file optional, no check that the reviewer UUID differs from the worker UUIDs). Two validators for one artifact will drift; export accepts a review that the controller would reject (a worker reviewing itself) and vice versa. PR 11 extracted one `check_review(review, bundle, digest, require_approved=)` used by both Pipeline.validate_review and ExportRuntime, and its CLI test proves the export refuses a worker-as-reviewer record.
findings.evidence: /home/agentops/dev/md-manager-high/workflow/pipeline.py:329-342 `def validate_review(self, review)` vs :421-444 `def validate_review_record(directory, plan, review)` (independent copies of the required-key set, the independence check and the finding loop; :432 has no `review["reviewer"] in worker_ids` check). PR 11 /home/agentops/dev/md-manager-ultra/workflow/pipeline.py:47-70 `def check_review(...)`, :385-387 `validate_review` delegates to it, :438 ExportRuntime calls `check_review(..., require_approved=False)`; test_export.py:269-274 expects "Independent reviewer identity required" from the export CLI.

findings.title: Handoff and completion files are passed into the export unvalidated
findings.detail: `"handoff": optional_json(directory / f"{node}.handoff.json")` copies whatever JSON is in the file. In manual mode `freeze` writes that file verbatim from an operator-supplied path, so arbitrary keys/values enter run-state.json, while the contract expects a strict `{summary, open_assumptions}`. `completion` is likewise untyped (`completion.get(key)` for three keys). PR 11 shapes both (`accepted_handoff`, `completion_signal`) and nulls anything malformed.
findings.evidence: /home/agentops/dev/md-manager-high/workflow/export_state.py:97-98; main /home/agentops/dev/md-manager/workflow/pipeline.py:552-554 `save_json(directory / f"{node}.handoff.json", read_json(handoff_path))`; contracts/projects/v1.ts `handoff: z.strictObject({ summary: z.string().min(1), open_assumptions: z.array(z.string().min(1)) }).nullable()`. PR 11 export_state.py:104-114.

findings.title: Inconsistent timestamp normalisation inside one file
findings.detail: The review section's `session.launch_requested_at` is copied raw (receipts store `+00:00`), while the inputs section's `launch.launch_requested_at` goes through `iso()` and becomes `Z`. `native_started_at` is normalised in both. A consumer gets two spellings of the same receipt field depending on section.
findings.evidence: /home/agentops/dev/md-manager-high/workflow/export_state.py:64 `session = {key: launch.get(key) for key in ("session_id", "background_id", "status", "launch_requested_at", ...)}` vs :95 `"launch_requested_at": iso(launch.get("launch_requested_at"))`.

findings.title: Dead null-policy branch and whole-file hashing
findings.detail: `export_run` reads policy.json unconditionally, so the `policy is None -> inputs None` branch is reachable only from a direct unit call (which the test does); the CLI can never produce `inputs: null`. The diff hash uses `hashlib.sha256(patch.read_bytes())` on a file that is 289 KB for the live run and unbounded in general, where PR 11 streams with `hashlib.file_digest`.
findings.evidence: /home/agentops/dev/md-manager-high/workflow/pipeline.py:463 `policy = validate_pipeline_policy(read_json(directory / "policy.json"))`; export_state.py:75-76, :61; test_export.py:150 calls `export_inputs(..., None)` directly. PR 11 export_state.py:84-85 `hashlib.file_digest(handle, "sha256")`.

findings.title: Solid export tests and helpers: real driven fixture downgraded to a 1.0.0 shape, lock, idempotence, truncation
findings.detail: The fixture drives the fake pipeline to completion and then strips it to the first live run's shape (no transport key, findings without link fields, version 1.0.0) before re-exporting through the CLI on a copy without worktrees; the lock test holds run_lock in-process and asserts the subprocess is refused and no session started; idempotence is byte-level; truncation and blocked verdict are covered. `iso()` handles both epoch-ms and offset strings; `optional_json` refuses symlinks.
findings.evidence: /home/agentops/dev/md-manager-high/workflow/test_export.py:45-61 `downgrade_to_1_0_0`, :92-113 (`ignore_patterns("worktree-*", "candidate", "review-worktree", ...)`, `assertEqual(read_bytes(), before)`), :127-134 ("Another controller owns this run", `sessions.starts == ["adapter","ui"]`), :152-159; export_state.py:33-44.

findings.title: Compatibility proven end to end: 1.0.0 runs still load, re-exported 1.2.0 runs serve review and inputs
findings.detail: The adapter accepts all three export versions and treats `review`/`inputs` as optional-nullable, so the on-disk project-workflows-001 loads unchanged and shows explicit 404 codes on the new routes, and after `workflow export` the same run serves its verdict, six findings, the hash-registered diff artifact and both workers' inputs. I reproduced this on a scratchpad copy with PR 11's own `workflow export` and its real adapter; the adapter test suite covers the same matrix (1.0.0 has neither, 1.1.0 review only, explicit nulls).
findings.evidence: /home/agentops/dev/md-manager-ultra/server/projects.ts `const EXPORT_VERSIONS = ['1.0.0', '1.1.0', '1.2.0'] as const`, `version: z.enum(EXPORT_VERSIONS)`, `review: reviewSectionSchema.nullable().optional()`, `inputs: inputsSectionSchema.nullable().optional()`. Commands: `PYTHONPATH=/home/agentops/dev/md-manager-ultra .venv/bin/python -m workflow export <copy>` -> "Exported run-state.json version 1.2.0 ... No agents launched." exit 0. tsx probe with PR 11 adapter: 1.0.0 copy -> `200 runs`, `200 detail (review node session_id null)`, `404 REVIEW_NOT_FOUND`, `404 INPUTS_NOT_FOUND`; re-exported copy -> `200 detail review_node session_id dd7bdcd1-... result_uri .../reviews/1`, `200 reviews/1 verdict=approved transport=print findings=6 diff artifact patch-review-2bb474561d3e`, `200 inputs mode=automatic ... reviewer_transport=print workers=ui:5418,adapter:4578`. server/projects.test.ts:1049-1081.

findings.title: Null handling and refusal paths are explicit, unified and tested
findings.detail: Optional receipts that are absent, symlinked, non-regular or malformed become null (`load_optional` catches ValueError; each shaper returns None on a type mismatch). The reviewer transport is taken from the plan, else from the receipts the run actually left, else null, never a default, and both sections agree. ExportRuntime refuses a changed policy, a bad automatic block, a review that names another candidate, and review.json without its bundle; a refused CLI export leaves the previous file untouched. One `check_review` serves controller and export.
findings.evidence: /home/agentops/dev/md-manager-ultra/workflow/export_state.py:43-50, :62-68, :93-121, :148; pipeline.py:415-440, :47-70; test_export.py:108-147 (malformed completion `{not json` -> None, manual plan -> `automatic: None`), :149-176 transport matrix incl. `assertIsNone(... ["reviewer_transport"])`, :226-257 refusal matrix, :259-275 CLI lock + "Independent reviewer identity required" + `assertEqual(read_json(...), exported)`.

findings.title: Transport is inferred from file existence, ignoring the receipt's own `transport` field
findings.detail: `recorded_transport` returns 'native' if review.interactive.json exists, else 'print' if automatic-review.json exists. But `_review_native` writes automatic-review.json with `transport: "native"` before `launch_reviewer` creates review.interactive.json; if the launch fails before the interactive receipt exists (the needs_reconciliation path), a plan without `reviewer_transport` exports `inputs.automatic.reviewer_transport: "print"` for a run that attempted a native review. Reading `receipt.get("transport")` first (as PR 10 does) would be both simpler and correct; the file-existence inference only exists to serve the one pre-slice-A receipt that lacks the field.
findings.evidence: /home/agentops/dev/md-manager-ultra/workflow/export_state.py:62-68; automatic.py:295-297 `receipt = {"transport": "native", ...}; save_json(receipt_path, receipt)` then :299 `runtime.launch_reviewer(...)`, :321-325 `except BaseException ... status="needs_reconciliation"`; automatic.py:58-60 legacy plans default to native so this path is reachable. Live receipt keys (no transport): `session_id, bundle_sha256, candidate_commit, status, patch_sha256, pid, review`.

findings.title: `stop.confirmed_at` is file mtime, which the docstring's 'copied run still exports' promise does not preserve
findings.detail: The export presents the stop marker's mtime as a confirmation time. That is a reasonable proxy for the original directory, but a `cp -r` copy (no `-p`) re-stamps it, so the same run exports different evidence from a copy. PR 10 instead writes `stopped_at` into the marker for new runs and exports null for old ones, which is more honest. Both PRs also fall back to mtime for `reviewed_at` when no event/receipt time exists.
findings.evidence: /home/agentops/dev/md-manager-ultra/workflow/export_state.py:121 `"confirmed_at": utc(path.stat().st_mtime) if item["stopped"] else None`; pipeline.py:416-419 docstring "a copied or finished run whose worktrees are gone still exports". PR 10 pipeline.py:155 `intent["stopped_at"] = now()`, export_state.py:100.

findings.title: `inputs_section` indexes policy keys the validator does not require, and ExportRuntime copies Pipeline.__init__
findings.detail: `policy["feature"]` and `policy["version"]` are read without a guard although `validate_policy` checks neither; a policy lacking them would raise KeyError from report() (a traceback, not the CLI's 'Blocked:' message). All shipped policies carry both, so this is latent. Separately, `ExportRuntime.__init__` restates the plan/automatic/policy-digest checks from `Pipeline.__init__` rather than sharing a helper, the same duplication PR 10's `export_run` has, just wrapped in a class; both PRs also restate prepare's 'never started' SimpleNamespace state.
findings.evidence: /home/agentops/dev/md-manager-ultra/workflow/export_state.py:142 `"feature": policy["feature"], "policy_version": policy["version"]`; main verification.py:48-71 `validate_policy` (no feature/version check; `check["scenarios"]` is required at :66 so that index is safe). pipeline.py:112-123 vs :422-433; :451 vs :625 `SimpleNamespace(values={}, next=("launch_ui", "launch_adapter"), tasks=[])`. PR 10 pipeline.py:447-471.

findings.title: Truncation placement: PR 11 keeps the export lossless and bounds at the adapter; PR 10 cuts inside the private record
findings.detail: PR 10 truncates task text to 256 KiB bytes in run-state.json (`decode(errors="ignore")` plus marker, `task_truncated` flag) and leaves path redaction to a future adapter. PR 11 exports the full task and the recorded prompt, and the adapter redacts first and then bounds at 64 KiB characters with a surrogate-safe cut and a marker that counts what was dropped, so the verbatim requirement-quote lookup runs on the full text and no cut can expose a partial path. PR 11's placement is the better separation of evidence from presentation; PR 10's is acceptable but loses text from the exported record (plan.json still has it).
findings.evidence: PR 10 export_state.py:17-18, :81-83; contracts/projects/v1.ts `task_truncated: z.boolean()`. PR 11 export_state.py:127-128 (`task`, `prompt`), server/projects.ts `const TEXT_LIMIT = 65536`, `function boundedText(raw)` (redactPaths then cut, marker `[… truncated by the viewer API: N more characters]`), `lanesQuoting` requires the quote to survive in `boundedText(text).text`; server/projects.test.ts:1089-1114.

findings.title: The two 1.2.0 export shapes are mutually incompatible
findings.detail: Both PRs call their export 1.2.0 but the section shapes differ (PR 10: `review.reviewer`, `review.session`, `inputs.workers` as a list with `task_truncated`/`stopped`/`stopped_at`, `feature` nullable; PR 11: `review.reviewer_session_id`, `inputs.workers` keyed by lane with `prompt`/`stop{stopped,confirmed_at}`, `policy_version`, `failure_drill`). Relevant only if pieces of both branches are combined: PR 11's adapter rejects PR 10's export outright.
findings.evidence: Probe, PR 11 adapter serving PR 10's export: `500 RUN_STORAGE_INVALID ... review.reviewer_session_id: Invalid input: expected string, received undefined; review: Unrecognized keys: "reviewer", "session"; inputs.feature: Invalid input: expected string, received null`. Field lists from the two probe dumps: PR 10 review keys `[attempt, bundle_sha256, candidate_commit, diff, findings, independent, reviewed_at, reviewer, session, transport, verdict]`; PR 11 `[..., reviewer_session_id, transport, verdict]`.

findings.title: Compatibility preserved by leaving the export and adapter untouched, as the umbrella PRD prescribes for slice A
findings.detail: PR 9 changes nothing under workflow/export_state.py, server/ or contracts/projects, so both the existing run and any new run export and load at 1.0.0 exactly as on main. The cost is that nothing new is visible (no review section, no `workflow export`), but the umbrella PRD assigns that to slice B's run. There is no compat risk to report.
findings.evidence: `git diff 61e4752 99c770f --stat -- workflow/export_state.py server/ src/ contracts/projects/` -> empty. main export_state.py:38 `"version": "1.0.0"`; main server/projects.ts:52 `version: z.literal(EXPORT_VERSION)`. Probe: main adapter + on-disk 1.0.0 run -> `200 runs=[["project-workflows-001","paused"]]`, `200 detail`. docs/PRD_REVIEW_VISIBILITY.md: ship A alone, B's feature run adds the review section and `workflow export`.
